bullets.title: Semis/Tech in freefall: SOX -27% in 5 weeks, 2028 estimate cuts needed to clear
bullets.body: The SOX index is down 27% over five weeks and broad tech is off ~18%, with buyside unlikely to add risk until 2028 EPS estimates are cut 15-20% — the earliest such cuts are expected in 1H27. NVDA buyside FY28 EPS estimates already down ~20% to ~$20, with ASIC competition and gross margin pressure as the key fears; tonight's earnings are unlikely to dispel those concerns even if FY27 guidance holds at ~70% growth.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO saga: Huang says 'honored to return'; board not considering reinstatement
bullets.body: Jensen Huang issued his first public statement since resigning, saying he would be 'honored' to return as CEO if the board decides it's in shareholders' best interest. Prediction markets put Huang's probability at 17% (up from 8% Friday), behind ARM's Rene Haas at 20%; the board is reportedly not considering reinstatement and Treasury Secretary Bessent is pushing for an external hire. The leadership overhang is limiting forward guidance visibility and accelerating bipartisan chip-export restrictions.

bullets.title: China optical transceiver ban advancing — COHR, LITE, FN rally 5-8% premarket
bullets.body: The Trump administration is moving forward with a ban on Chinese optical transceivers; China represents two-thirds of the global optical market. COHR and LITE each jumped 5-8% premarket on the news, though one analyst cautioned the ban is likely phased in from 2029 and excludes legacy speeds, making the rally potentially premature.

bullets.title: New NVDA chip-export rule: overseas data centers must license remote chip rentals
bullets.body: The US Commerce Department issued an interim rule blocking overseas data centers from remotely renting NVIDIA chips without a license; a separate new rule requires due diligence on high-risk nations, effective in 90 days. NVDA's Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the House on Dec 1, with General Counsel on Dec 2.

bullets.title: Macro regime shift warning: Hedgeye/OPCO flag 'Quad 4' — GDP set to halve to 1.4% in Q1 2027
bullets.body: Both Hedgeye and Oppenheimer macro strategists flag a regime shift to 'Quad 4' (decelerating growth + decelerating inflation), the worst setup for risk assets. Hedgeye's GDP Nowcast peaks at 3.48% in Q4 2026 before potentially halving to 1.40% in Q1 2027. Cross-asset signals — dollar at 52-week highs, commodities breaking down, curve flattening on hawkish front-end repricing — confirm the setup; strategy shifts from 'buy dips' to 'sell rallies.'

bullets.title: October retail sales beat: control group +0.6% m/m; Q4 PCE tracking raised to 2.1-2.5%
bullets.body: October control-group retail sales came in at +0.6% m/m vs. +0.3% consensus, with August and September each revised up ~37bp. Morgan Stanley raised its Q4 consumption tracking to 2.1% q/q annualized (from 1.6%), while a separate economist raised PCE tracking to ~2.5%, well above Bloomberg consensus of ~2%. E-commerce accelerated to +11.8% y/y; weakness was concentrated in autos (-1.6%), clothing, and sporting goods.

bullets.title: Core PCE inflation on track to re-accelerate: MS forecasts +0.30% m/m, 3.22% y/y in October
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley forecasts October core PCE at +0.30% m/m (headline +0.32%), pushing the year-over-year rate to 3.22% from 3.10% in September — the third consecutive upside surprise. The 3-month annualized pace rises to 3.49% vs. 2.82% prior, complicating any near-term Fed easing narrative. Market is now pricing 22bp of Fed hikes through year-end 2027, up 13bp week-over-week.

bullets.title: Housing hits 14-year low: NAHB falls to 25 in November, all regions and components decline
bullets.body: The November NAHB Housing Market Index dropped 4 points to 25, the lowest reading since 2012. All three sub-components (current sales, prospective buyer traffic, and future sales expectations) and all four geographic regions declined, reinforcing the view that elevated rates are decisively weighing on residential construction activity.

bullets.title: Industrial production soft in October, but AI-related hardware output strong: semis +2.2%, computers +3.2%
bullets.body: Headline industrial production fell 0.4% m/m in October, below the 0.1% consensus, dragged by a -4.3% m/m drop in mining and utilities. However, AI-linked manufacturing bucked the trend: semiconductors +2.2% m/m, computer equipment +3.2% m/m, and communications equipment +0.9% m/m — consistent with ongoing hyperscaler capex.

bullets.title: Financial conditions tightening moderately; daily unsmoothed FCI shows more than official lagged index
bullets.body: An analyst's real-time, unsmoothed version of the Fed's Financial Conditions Index shows more tightening than the official lagged measure (last observation December, 3-month smoothed). Asset prices at current levels would reflect moderate — but not dramatic — tightening if held flat for three months, suggesting conditions are becoming a headwind but not yet a shock.

bullets.title: Active funds added AI holdings at a record pace in 3Q, even as tech exposure overall dropped
bullets.body: Median share increases across Morgan Stanley's AI Index constituents hit a historical high of 14.4% in Q3, with hyperscalers seeing the largest additions. Notably, broad Technology sector exposure continued to fall, suggesting active managers are discriminating — concentrating in AI names while reducing non-AI tech. Names with the largest quarterly share increases generated rolling 6-month excess returns of 3.1-3.9%.

bullets.title: MSFT global outage traced to undetected July bug; autonomous AI cyberattacks now operational
bullets.body: Microsoft's recent global outage — which left 80% of Outlook servers unresponsive for 15 hours — was caused by an undetected bug present since July. Separately, Google's AI Threat Tracker confirms autonomous LLM-driven attacks are now operational, with zero-day exploits spiking to 22 in August 2026 vs. an 8/month average in 2025, and cyber incidents doubling to 105 in the final two weeks of October.

bullets.title: Cyber insurance rates set to jump 25-75% in 6 months as AI-driven losses mount
bullets.body: After roughly four years of soft pricing, enterprise cyber insurance loss ratios are deteriorating sharply as AI accelerates attack frequency and severity. Pricing is expected to rise 25-75% within six months; the MSFT outage alone generated an estimated $400M-$1.5B in insured losses. The cybersecurity equity index (HACK) is paradoxically down 15% from its November highs despite fundamental deterioration.

bullets.title: US equity recovery largely short covering, not long accumulation; Russell 2000 remains bearishly positioned
bullets.body: Citi notes the recent US equity bounce has been driven predominantly by short covering rather than fresh long flows. The Russell 2000 remains at extended bearish exposure levels. The S&P 500 needs to reclaim ~7,600 to break the negative gamma backdrop; current support is near 7,300 with a tail-risk scenario at 7,000.

bullets.title: Semiconductor double-counting risk emerging as multiple chip vendors plan independently with same AI model providers
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags a growing concern that semiconductor demand is being double-counted: multiple chip vendors are now planning independently with the same AI model providers, creating the risk that forward order books overstate true end-demand. NAND spot prices have already fallen 20% in two weeks on GPU shortages and weak consumer electronics demand, with YMTC competition adding pressure.

bullets.title: JPM 2025 global GDP weights updated: US 28.8%, China falls to 18.4%, Euro area gains most
bullets.body: JPMorgan's updated 2025 global GDP weight table shows the Euro area posted the largest gain (+0.5pp), while China fell 0.4pp to 18.4% (down from a 2021 peak of ~19%) due to deflation and weak domestic demand. The US lost 0.45pp despite remaining the world's largest economy. JPM holds its 2026-27 global growth forecast steady at 2.7%, with long-run potential growth raised 0.2pp to 2.4%.

bullets.title: Eurozone investor sentiment near cycle highs; ECB pricing 50bp of tightening through April 2027
bullets.body: German ZEW Expectations rose 7.5 points to 35.6 and the Eurozone measure rose 8.0 to 26.5, with the DAX and STOXX trading near record highs and recently outperforming the S&P. However, Piper Sandler's models forecast cooler activity ahead from lagged rate impacts; markets have priced 50bp of ECB tightening through April 2027, and structural headwinds (aging demographics, weak productivity, energy dependence) remain.

bullets.title: BXDC's $5B AWS sale-leaseback debut: 7% cap rate, 647 MW across 13 assets, nearly all IPO proceeds deployed
bullets.body: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust closed its inaugural deal — a $5B AWS sale-leaseback covering 647 MW across 13 assets at a 7% cap rate with 2.75% annual rent escalators, deploying nearly all IPO proceeds at ~49% LTV (above the 40% target). Morgan Stanley maintains Equal-weight at a $23 YE27 target, noting the powered-shell assets were valued at $7.7M/MW vs. $15M/MW IPO expectations for turnkey assets, limiting comparability with future deals.

bullets.title: Kalshi acquires FB Securities for stock trading launch; HOOD down 7% on competitive threat
bullets.body: Prediction market platform Kalshi acquired FB Securities to launch into stock trading, posing a direct competitive threat to Robinhood. HOOD fell 7% on the news.

bullets.title: Bitcoin -48% from ATH, -22% last month; speculative bubble unwind accelerating across risk assets
bullets.body: Bitcoin is down 48% from its all-time high and 22% over the past month. Hedgeye notes the retail sentiment basket crashed from +22% YTD to -21%, profitless tech fell 4.6% in a single session, and the KOSPI is down 45% from its peak in the current Quad 4 regime. The pattern is consistent with a broad speculative bubble unwind across leveraged and momentum exposures.
